title: Numerical evaluation of one-loop integrals using quadrature rules
description: finite one-loop scalar pentagon with off-shell spacelike legs and massive lines, 'Euclidean' kinematics
mapping_notes: Routing from the authors' code src/problems/pentagon.py (E1..E5). Four-momenta (E,px,py,pz) from Table 3 (identical to src/setups/pentagon.py) rationalized exactly as printed decimals; p5 = -(p1+..+p4). external_gram[i][j] = p_i.p_j with metric (+,-,-,-). mass_squared = (printed m)^2 exactly.
reference_combination: I_paper = i int d^4k/pi^2 prod 1/(q_i^2-m_i^2+i0) = (-1)^{N+1} I_DiffExp = +I_DiffExp for N=5 (eps^0, d=4; integral is finite)
normalization: Paper eq.(1): I = i int d^D k / pi^{D/2} N/(D_1...D_N), D_i = q_i^2 - m_i^2 + i eps. Converts to DiffExp with factor (-1)^{N+1}; check: their triangles (N=3) and pentagons are positive, boxes negative, consistent.
confidence: high; residual mismatch ~1e-16 relative possible because LoopTools/hp were fed double-precision invariants computed from these decimals
check: vs paper: pentagon (LoopTools quad) 16 digits (1 orders)
